transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello. Well... I suppose it's about bridges. If it turns out I absolutely have to cross one, if there's no way around it... my heart just starts pounding right away. My hands get all damp on the steering wheel or the armrest. It's... just a terrible rush of fear. Even before I'm actually on the thing. So... that's why I'm here.
Do you experience this kind of fear in situations other than crossing bridges?
No... no, it's just the bridges. Everything else is fine.
Is your fear of bridges related to the height of the bridge?

Yes... I suppose so. The high ones, mostly. I mean... I know perfectly well that thousands of cars cross those bridges every day without any trouble. But... when I see a high span on the map, or coming up ahead through the windshield... it just feels like... like the whole thing is waiting to drop away under us.
Is your fear of being on a high bridge because you're afraid of falling?
I... I don't know if I'd call it that. I haven't really... thought about it in those exact terms. It's just... being up there. That's all.
Do you experience a similar fear when you are in other high places, such as tall buildings or mountains?
No, I... I don't think so. Tall buildings don't bother me. Just... just the bridges.
Are you afraid of being on the bridge when you're not moving, such as if you were to stop your car on the bridge?
I don't know. I... I try not to stop on them. I just want to get across.
Are you afraid of walking across a bridge, or is your fear mainly related to driving across it?
I don't really know. I... I haven't walked across one in a long time. I just prefer to stay off them altogether.
Would your fear be the same if you were a passenger on a bridge, rather than the one driving?
I suppose so. I... I just don't want to be on them at all. It doesn't really matter who's at the wheel.
Have you ever had a traumatic experience involving a bridge?
No. I... not that I can remember. Nothing like that happened. I just... I don't know why I'm like this with them.
Is it the sight of the bridge itself that triggers your fear, rather than just the knowledge that you have to cross it?

I suppose seeing it makes it worse. I... I know perfectly well that thousands of cars cross those bridges every day. But if I see a high span coming up ahead through the windshield... or even just see one drawn on a map... it just feels to me like the whole thing is waiting to drop away under us. So... yes, seeing it is hard.
Is your fear of bridges more about the act of crossing over the bridge, or is it just being on the bridge in general?
I don't really know. I... I haven't thought about it like that. Being on it, crossing it... it's all the same to me. I just don't want to be on them.
Is there something specific about the bridge's structure, like the material or the design, that triggers your fear?
I don't think so. I haven't really... paid attention to the designs or what they're made of. It's just... the bridge itself.
Do you worry that the bridge might collapse while you're on it?
No, I... I don't really think about it falling apart or breaking. It's not that. I just... I don't know. I just don't want to be up there.
Is your fear of bridges only about the act of crossing over it, or would you feel the same fear if you were just standing under a high bridge?
I couldn't tell you. I... I don't make a habit of standing under them. I just stay away.
Is your fear of bridges less intense when you cross lower bridges, such as those over small streams?
I... I really couldn't say. A bridge is a bridge to me. I just... I don't cross them. Doesn't really matter how high they are, I just stay away.
Do you think your fear of bridges would decrease if you were accompanied by someone you trust, such as a close friend or family member?

No. It doesn't decrease it. If I absolutely have to cross one, I... I do need someone with me, yes. But I just sit there frightened the whole way across anyway. 

I'd rather just not do it. For over two years now, I've just been planning my errands around avoiding them entirely. I gave up trips to the San Juans, Seattle theater nights... I just stay away. If I absolutely must go, I have to study the route, get the timing just so... and have someone there. But no, it doesn't make me less afraid.
Would your fear be less if you were able to magically be on the other side of the bridge without actually crossing it?
I suppose so. If I didn't have to cross it... then I wouldn't have to cross it. But that's not how it works, is it?
Would your fear be present if you were somehow already on the bridge, without having to cross it to get there?
I don't... I don't know. I've never been just dropped onto a bridge out of nowhere. I suppose I'd still be terrified because I'd still be on it. But I don't really like thinking about it.
Would your fear of the bridge be present if you were somehow already on the other side of the bridge, without having to cross it to get there?

I... didn't you just ask me that? 

If I'm already on the other side... well, I'm not on the bridge anymore. So, no. I suppose I wouldn't be afraid then. I just... I don't really see the point of these questions.
